new: People in a headset are drawn as whole bodies with legs and feet: a mannequin in street armour in their own colour, posed from their headset and controllers.
Their feet stay planted and step as they walk; with the sticks (faster than walking) they glide. In AR only people elsewhere get a body.
My body (the menu's Settings tab, under Frame rate; off by default): your own body when you look down, in VR, in a room or not. Never sent.
Bodies: on / off (the Debug tab, This headset, beside People): off draws heads and hands as before. Each headset's own.
Studio: a model's Animation can be As it moves: its walk clip follows the distance it covers (on a path, a behaviour, a motion or carried), and it stands still when it stops.
As it moves has a Standing clip (or Still) and Stride: Shorter, Longer and As measured. Rooms move to format networks-53.
test: Two headsets in a room: walk round each other; the other's body stands, steps and turns with them, its hands where their controllers are.
Look down with My body on; then off. Try it with Bodies off on one headset (heads and hands) and on the other.
Move with the sticks: the other's body glides, then plants its feet when they stop. Crouch, lean, look down.
On a phone or a laptop following a room (or the preview camera): people show as bodies; the name sign sits just over the helmet.
Studio: open the walks test scene, or give a rigged walker As it moves and a recorded path; scrub its path and watch the walk follow.
untested: Everything on a real headset: how the bodies look and move at full frame rate, how your own arms follow real controllers, comfort looking down.
The cost with many people (48 bodies) on a Quest; one draw for all bodies was measured only here.
AR passthrough behind the bodies (the test session shows no room).
Studio walkers beside you in a headset: turning, crossfades and how far their feet slide.
